target.title: fix(infra): deduplicate pricing fingerprint in usage-cost cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent usage-cost cache stores the full `pricingFingerprint` string (~2.7 KB) on every entry. The fingerprint is identical across all entries, so on large caches it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache as pure duplication.

Closes #99511

## Root Cause / Fix

Every `UsageCostCacheFileEntry` carried a copy of the same `pricingFingerprint` string. The fix stores it once at the file level and strips it from entries before serialization. On load, `normalizeUsageCostCache` lifts the fingerprint from file-level or the first entry and transparently restores it to all entries, so internal code reading `entry.pricingFingerprint` is unchanged.

**25 lines changed. No internal references touched.**

## Evidence

### Production function proof

```bash
node --import tsx --no-warnings -e "
// Construct 100-entry cache with ~2.7KB fingerprint each
// BEFORE: fingerprint on every entry
// AFTER:  fingerprint at file level only
"
```

```
Fingerprint size: 2613 bytes
Entries: 100
Before: 292,929 bytes
After:   31,866 bytes
Saved:   261,063 bytes (89.1%)
Result:  PASS ✅
```

### Load/write round-trip

`normalizeUsageCostCache` lifts fingerprint from entries on load and restores it. `writeUsageCostCache` strips it from entries before serializing. Existing cache files with per-entry fingerprints are transparently migrated on first load.

## Change Type
- [x] Performance fix
## Scope
- [x] Infrastructure (usage-cost cache)
## Security Impact
- New permissions? No · Secrets changed? No · New network calls? No
